loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

tools.name: SubagentHandback

The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

## 1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai .../artifact/... link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{...}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). # Issue #18 verification: Refine version arrows

Issue [#18](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/18). Checked on 2026-10-29 in a real browser (`agent-browser`, headless Chrome) against `pnpm dev`, with `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` ([ADR 0010](../adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md)) through the Vite proxy, on the sample Document. 1440 x 900 for the margin card, 1100 x 900 for the floating Card.

The Active Suggestion's Card shows `‹ n / m ›` and the shown step's Instruction once its `history` has 2 or more steps. `ReadySuggestion` gains `shown`, the index of the shown step; `replacement`, `rationale` and `diff` mirror that step, so Accept and the decorations read them unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| TDD covers showing a version and Refine from an earlier version | Pass | `src/suggestions/state.test.ts`: `showVersion` (newest step after each Refine; `replacement`, `rationale` and `diff` follow the shown step, diff against the original; bounds `-1`, `3`, `0.5`; same step; ignored while refining; after a failed Refine it steps and dismisses the error, so Retry has nothing to re-run; unknown, pending and error Suggestions; other Suggestions untouched), Refine from an earlier step (success cuts the later steps and appends; "no change" keeps them; failure keeps them; retry then success cuts; cancel keeps them), `instructionHistory` stops at the shown step. `src/editor/suggestion-runtime.test.ts`: the request from `1/3` carries only the first Instruction and its Replacement, then the history is `[first, new]`. `src/editor/suggestion-cards.test.ts`: arrows absent with one step, present from 2, follow the shown step, locked while refining, absent on the hover card. `pnpm test`: 660 tests green |
| The arrows show only with 2 or more steps, and fit the margin card (256px) and the floating Card | Pass | One step: Accept / Reject / Refine only. Margin card: [18-1](img/18-1.png), the arrow row is 243px wide inside the 256px card, a long Instruction ends in an ellipsis ([18-3](img/18-3.png)). Floating Card: [18-5](img/18-5.png) |
| Stepping updates the inline diff, the Rationale and the counter in place; the diff stays against the original | Pass | `3 / 3` → `2 / 3` → `1 / 3` with clicks: the counter, the Instruction ("use a warmer tone", "make it shorter", "More formal"), the Rationale and the inserted text change; the struck text is the original paragraph every time. [18-1](img/18-1.png) then [18-2](img/18-2.png). A mouse click leaves focus in the text |
| Accept applies the shown version, `Ctrl+Z` restores the original | Pass | At `1 / 2`, Accept: the paragraph is the `1 / 2` Replacement, no Card left ([18-4](img/18-4.png)). `Ctrl+Z`: the original paragraph is back |
| A Refine from `1/3` sends only the Instructions up to `1/3` and its Replacement, and the result replaces `2/3` and `3/3` | Pass | Request body below. The answer gives `2 / 2` with the new Instruction "say we now deploy on weekdays" ([18-3](img/18-3.png)); stepping back gives `1 / 2` "More formal" |
| The arrows are disabled while refining and reachable with Tab | Pass | During each Refine the snapshot shows `Previous version [disabled]`, `Next version [disabled]` and `Refining… [disabled]`. At `1 / 3`, `Tab` from the text focuses "Next version" (Previous is disabled). `Enter` steps to `2 / 3` with focus kept; `Enter` again reaches `3 / 3`, Next turns disabled and focus moves to "Previous version"; `Enter` gives `2 / 3` |
| ADR 0007 is amended and `docs/BACKLOG.md` drops the item | Pass | [ADR 0007](../adr/0007-suggestion-lifecycle.md), [BACKLOG.md](../../BACKLOG.md) |
| AI call records and screenshots are here, `ai-costs.md` is updated | Pass | This file and [ai-costs.md](../ai-costs.md) |

Extra checks:
- **A failed Refine drops nothing.** With `window.fetch` failing the model call (no request reached OpenRouter), a Refine from `1 / 2` showed "Could not reach the model…" with Retry and kept both steps ([18-7](img/18-7.png)); `Esc` dismissed it and both steps stayed.
- **Stepping dismisses a failed Refine's error** (review fix). Without it, a Retry after stepping re-sent the failed Instruction on top of another version. After the fix, on a reloaded page with a 2-step Suggestion injected through the suggestion effects (no model call): a forced failure at `2 / 2`, then "Previous version" gives `1 / 2`, its Rationale, and no error or Retry ([18-8](img/18-8.png)). The only record is that forced failure (`refine p4 → fail please`, error).
- **The Refine input survives a version step.** Typing "abc" in the Refine input, then clicking "Previous version": focus stays in the input with "abc", the counter reads `1 / 2`, and the next key types into it ([18-6](img/18-6.png)). The Card now updates its children in place (`syncChildren` in `src/editor/dom.ts`) instead of replacing them all, so the input and the arrow row stay in the page; the old refocus step for the input went away with it.
- **"No change" adds no step.** "keep the ten percent rollout detail" came back equal to the shown Replacement: no new step, no arrows (the existing `resolveRefine` rule).

18:- **Versions:** once a Suggestion has 2 or more steps (the first request plus each Refine), its Card shows `‹ n / m ›` with the shown step's Instruction. The arrows switch the shown Replacement, its Rationale and the inline diff; Accept applies the shown version. The original text is not a version: Reject covers it. A Refine from an earlier version sends only the Instructions up to it, with its Replacement as the latest; on success the later steps are dropped and the new one is appended, like typing after an undo. A failed or cancelled Refine drops nothing; stepping to another version dismisses a failed Refine's error, so Retry always repeats the same request. The arrows are disabled while a Refine is in flight. With the cursor inside such a Suggestion, `Ctrl+H` / `Ctrl+L` show the previous / next version (`Ctrl` on macOS too, since `Cmd+H` hides the app). They are free in CodeMirror outside macOS, and the browser's History and address bar keys are kept away only there; on macOS they replace delete-backward and select-line, which would edit inside the Suggestion anyway. `Alt-ArrowLeft` / `Alt-ArrowRight` and `Mod-[` / `Mod-]` stay with CodeMirror (word or syntax jumps, indentation), and `Ctrl+Alt+arrows` is often taken by the desktop or VoiceOver.

input.message:
No bugs. Four minor findings. Read through git objects only. I did not run the code, so findings 1 and 4 come from reading it.

Checked and clean:
- An out-of-range index is a no-op. `showVersion` (state.ts) returns `state` unchanged for `history[-1]`, `history[len]`, the same index, or while refining. It only resets `refine` to idle on a real step.
- The command and the Card pick the same Suggestion. `suggestionAtCursor` and `activeSuggestion` both take the most recent one containing the cursor, and `acceptAtCursor` uses the same lookup.
- The commit message is `feat: Ctrl+H / Ctrl+L switch Refine versions`, with no trailer.
- No comments added, and names match GLOSSARY.md.
- README and ADR 0007 match the code.
- CodeMirror 6's defaults match the macOS claim: `Ctrl-h` is `deleteCharBackward`, and `Ctrl-l` is `selectLine` on macOS only.
- The 18-9 screenshot shows `1 / 2`, "First." and the tooltip, as the record says.

Findings:
1. suggestion-cards.ts:289 (and the `title` below it): `aria-keyshortcuts` and the `(Ctrl+H)` hint sit on the arrow buttons. The keymap only runs from the editor content. With focus on an arrow button (reached by Tab) or in the Refine input, the Card's keydown handler (suggestion-cards.ts:437) only handles Tab and Escape, so the key goes to the browser's History. The hint overstates where the key works.
2. ADR 0007:18: "select-line, which would edit inside the Suggestion anyway" is wrong for `Ctrl-l`, because `selectLine` doesn't edit. Only `Ctrl-h` does.
3. suggestion-keymap.test.ts: the end-of-range test only asserts `shown`. Nothing covers index -1 or the failed Refine error surviving the no-op.
4. suggestion-keymap.ts:59: `suggestionAtCursor` includes non-ready Suggestions. At a shared boundary with a newer pending Suggestion, the key returns false while the Card, which only considers ready ones, still shows arrows. This is the same behaviour as `acceptAtCursor`.
